_about: Three filled-in examples in the template format (see WRITING_GUIDE.md). 1: HS_014, a simple scenario. 2: HS_003, which starts a story chain through flags (helped_freshman / bullied_freshman, read by HS_034, HS_073, HS_094) and queues a follow-up two weeks later (HS_003F, a new follow-up-only scenario added by the import). 3: HS_005, Tyler Brooks's first scene: relationship changes and a choice locked behind the head coach's trust. They pass the importer (python3 tools/import_scenarios.py tools/authoring/examples.json --dry-run); import them for real only if you want them in the game.

scenarios.title: The Bad Weather Practice
scenarios.text: Sideways rain and a cold wind roll in an hour into practice. The coaches say kickers can stay out or head inside.

choices.label: Kick through the downpour
choices.result: Soaked and shivering, but you learned how a wet ball comes off your foot.

choices.label: Work on your form in the gym
choices.result: Slow-motion swings in front of the mirror. Less glamorous, cleaner technique.

choices.label: Call it a day early
choices.result: Hot shower, dry socks, early dinner. A couple of teammates notice you left.

scenarios.title: The Locker Room Joke
scenarios.text: A few upperclassmen hide a freshman's practice gear and the whole locker room is laughing at him as he searches for it.

choices.label: Step in and help him find it
choices.result: The laughing stops. A senior rolls his eyes, but the freshman won't forget it.

choices.label: Laugh along with everyone
choices.result: The upperclassmen clap you on the back. The freshman doesn't look at you again.

choices.label: Stay out of it
choices.result: You lace up and head to the field. Not your fight, you tell yourself.

scenarios.title: A Quiet Thank-You
scenarios.text: The freshman you stood up for catches you after practice. Nobody has hidden his gear since, and he wanted you to know he noticed.

choices.label: Invite him to sit with the team at lunch
choices.result: He's quiet at first. By Friday he's trading jokes with the linemen.

choices.label: Tell him to pay it forward
choices.result: He nods like it's a promise. You walk to your car a little taller.

scenarios.title: The First Rival
scenarios.text: {tyler}, the other freshman kicker, drills four straight from forty yards on the first day of practice and makes sure everyone, especially you, saw it.

choices.label: Ask him to work on kicks together
choices.result: He looks surprised, then shrugs. You split the net and trade tips until dark.

choices.label: Tell him the job is yours
choices.result: "We'll see," he says. It's on, and you've never been so motivated to practice.

choices.label: Ask {coach} to let you two compete in practice
choices.result: {coach} turns it into a weekly kicking ladder. You and {tyler} push each other, and respect each other.
